title: Choose the deck's visual world
question: The roll assigned Cairo Sign-Painter. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Cairo Sign-Painter
options.lineage: hand-painted Cairo shop fascias and microbus panels
options.thesis: Every slide is a painted shop sign: one message, read from across the street.
options.viewport: A red fascia carries the title in heavy caps with a black drop-shade; three colored price-board panels below; a white enamel rail holds slide number and section clock.
options.risk: Tips into tourist kitsch if the lettering gets ornamental instead of plain and heavy.

raised.raise: Pose and answer: each teaching slide pairs a claim panel with its live demo panel across one seam.
Ink budget: six paint tins, no tints, no gradients, no glow.
Every fact about a real winner carries its source line; demo numbers are labeled synthetic.
Fixed frame: the border and presenter rail never move; only panel contents change.
Label grid: every panel opens with the same header strip (number, section, minutes).

options.label: Tabletop Rulebook
options.thesis: The workshop is a game you play: setup, turns, rule tables, end condition.
options.viewport: Cobalt board with the title as the game's name; a white setup card lists the five spec pieces; a die token shows 3 variables.
options.risk: The direction most game-design talks land on; can read as playful over scientific.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The talk as a broadcast index: numbered pages, timed sections, hidden answers behind REVEAL.
options.viewport: P101 index page: title in double-height yellow, section pages listed with minutes, a red REVEAL key.
options.case: REVEAL fits ask-the-room moments and the grid projects sharply; loses on audience identification, teletext was never common in Egypt.
options.risk: Reads retro-novelty if the grid is not strict.

options.label: Bazaar Spread
options.thesis: Two-page spreads where image and headline answer each other.
options.viewport: A spread with a photo pose on the left and a hairline headline answering on the right.
options.case: Hairlines vanish on a projector and students don't identify with fashion editorial.
options.kept: Pose and answer: claim and live demo paired across one seam.

options.label: CD-ROM Console
options.thesis: A rendered console with a small live window in the middle.
options.viewport: A gray console frame around a small content window.
options.case: Shrinks the content into a postcard window; wrong for a projector.
options.kept: Fixed frame: chrome never moves, only contents change.

options.label: Risograph Print
options.thesis: Two or three spot inks misregistered on paper.
options.viewport: Fluoro pink and blue shapes overlapping on warm paper.
options.case: Fluorescent inks wash out on projectors and the paper ground is the cream default.
options.kept: Ink budget: a fixed small set of flat colors, nothing else.

options.label: Sneaker Box Wall
options.thesis: A wall of boxes indexed by end labels.
options.viewport: Stacked orange boxes with condensed labels.
options.case: No link to space data or game design.
options.kept: Label grid: every panel keyed by the same header strip.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: One ribbon tracing an object's custody.
options.viewport: A red ribbon running down an archival page.
options.case: A single-column archival form, wrong pace for a live workshop.
options.kept: Mark what's verified: sources on real facts, synthetic labels on demo data.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean conference keynote, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: White slide, big title, small blue kicker, footer with section and slide number.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other talk that day.
